questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Having worked for the whole day, you shall have taken some rest and begun again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**you shall have taken**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence, 'shall' is incorrect
 
• **'Shall' **is used for future tense but the sentence is in the past tense. 
 
• '**Should**' is the past tense of '**Shall**'.
 
• The correct word must be **'should'.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

__
 
• In error-type questions, we first look for grammatical errors if any and then vocabulary based errors.

 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Whenever **'Having' i**s used as a subject, past participle of the verb follows it. 
 
• **'Begun' i**s the past participle of the verb **'begin' **and **'began'** is the past tense of the same verb. 

 

​So the correct sentence is - *Having worked for the whole day, **you should have taken** some rest and begun again.*

As you can see from my resume, __I am working in Mumbai since 2016.__

options.text: I am work in Mumbai since 2016.
I am working in Mumbai from 2016.
I have been working in Mumbai since 2016.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The sentence says that his **work** in Mumbai is mentioned in his resume. 
 
• It says he is working in Mumbai since 2016. So, the sentence is in the **present perfect tense. **
 
• The **present perfect tense **is used to express a past event that has present consequences.
 
• '**have**' and '**has**' are used in the present perfect tense. '**been**' will be used because 'am' is mentioned. 
 
• So, 'I have been working in Mumbai since 2016' is the correct solution. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

__
 
• In error-type questions, we first look for grammatical errors if any and then vocabulary based errors.
 
• We look at the tense of the whole sentence and see if all the verbs are in the correct tense. 

 

So the correct sentence is - *As you can see from my resume, I have been working in Mumbai since 2016.__*

• In the sentence,** 'functioning for**' is incorrect. 
 
• Here, the preposition 'for' is used for saying who or what is intended to receive something or get the benefit of it.__

• In the sentence, parliamentary democracy is **related** to the State. So, '**of**' must be the correct preposition. 
 
• So, 'functioning of the State' is the correct solution. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

• We look at the tense of the whole sentence and see if all the verbs are in the correct tense. 

 

**So the correct sentence is - ***One could argue that these are the compulsions of parliamentary democracy for the smooth functioning **of** the State.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Context of the sentence:__ Here it is said that an individual keeps his fingers crossed because he expects best to happen. 
 
• Here, he has a **feeling** that if he crossed his fingers, best will happen. 
 
• In option 3, 'hopes' means __a feeling of expectation and desire for a particular thing to happen.__
 
• So, 'hopes' is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let us know the meanings of other given words:
 
 
• **reacts - **act in response to something; respond in a particular way.
 
• **suspects - **have an idea or impression of the existence, presence, or truth of (something) without certain proof.
 
• **responds - **say something in reply.

 
 
 

So the correct sentence is - *If an individual keeps his fingers crossed he **hopes** for the best.*

questions.question: **Select the correctly spelt word.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Sometimes it is necessary for an author to know what is going on in the minds of his ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**characters**​'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Context of the sentence:__ Here it is said that an author has to know whats going on with his individuals in his creation. 
 
• Here, the author wants to know what's going on in the minds of the individuals in his story. 
 
• In option 4, 'characters' means __the mental and moral qualities distinctive to an individual.__
 
• So, 'characters' is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• Let us know the meanings of other given words:
 
 
• **listeners - **a person who listens, especially someone who does so in an attentive manner.
 
• **viewers - **a person who looks at or inspects something.
 
• **audience - **the assembled spectators or listeners at a public event such as a play, film, concert, or meeting.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In the sentence, 'his' is used so it means the word in the blank **belongs** to the author. 
 
• Here, '**characters**' in the story belongs to its author. 
 
• Rest all other options do not belong to the author. 

 

So the correct sentence is - *Sometimes it is necessary for an author to know what is going on in the minds of his **character.***
